strategies.name: Nifty Expiry Day Selling
strategies.description: Open the position: Shortly after the market opens, once early volatility settles, sells a call and a put and buys farther-out options on both sides as protection. Earn through the session: Holds the hedged position to collect premium as the options lose value through the day. Switch for the final hour: Closes the first position and opens a tighter second one to capture the faster decay near expiry. Exit before close: Each sold option has its own stop-loss — 50% on each sell leg in the First setup and 70% in the Second setup* — and all positions are squared off before the market ends.

strategies.name: Bank Nifty Bearish Buying
strategies.description: Confirms the bearish trend: Uses Bollinger Bands, RSI, EMA, and CCI to check that Bank Nifty is under strong selling pressure. Validates participation: Confirms enough traded volume is behind the move before committing to a trade. Buys the put: Enters a Bank Nifty ATM put option once the signals line up. Manages the risk: Exits on SL or Target, whichever comes first. Actual exit price may vary slightly from what's set as SL or Target.

strategies.name: Trend Surge Buying
strategies.description: Confirm the trend: Checks that price is holding above the day's VWAP, showing genuine bullish strength. Validate the breakout: Confirms price has pushed above the previous day's high and the day's highest high before committing to a trade. Buy the call: Enters a Nifty call option around ₹200 premium once the trend and breakout both line up. Manage the risk: Exits when price closes below VWAP or the option loses 30%, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: Nifty Trend Catcher
strategies.description: Watches both directions: Uses Super Trend, Bollinger Bands, RSI, and CCI to monitor Nifty for either a bullish breakout or a bearish breakdown, and commits to whichever triggers first. Validates the move: Confirms the breakout past key Pivot Point levels and recent highs or lows before committing to a trade. Buys the option: Enters a call for a bullish move or a put for a bearish move, around 0.66 delta, once the signals line up. Manages the risk: Exits when Super Trend reverses or the option loses 10% of its value, whichever comes first. If the trade exits in a loss, a defined opposite-side trade may follow with double the initial quantity if the reversal trade is confirmed.

rules.name: Avoid calls outside a confirmed uptrend
rules.conditionText: Avoid CALL option entries when market regime shows RANGING, BEARISH or SIDEWAYS conditions. Empirical data from 52 CALL paper trades shows 34.6% aggregate win rate (20-24% in bearish/ranging markets) vs 51.3% on PUT trades in same period. STRONG_COUNTER_TREND failure pattern detected 14 times on vwap_pullback_v1. Only enter CALL when regime is confirmed TRENDING_UP with ADX > 20 and spot > VWAP.

evidence.justification: Empirical data from 52 CALL paper trades shows 34.6% aggregate win rate.

rules.name: Prefer puts over calls in sideways or bearish regimes
rules.conditionText: Prefer PUT option entries over CALL entries when market regime is RANGING, SIDEWAYS, or BEARISH. In confirmed downtrend or sideways conditions, PUT entries have demonstrated significantly higher win rates and positive net P&L.

evidence.justification: PUT win rate = 51.3% (net +7,089 INR) vs CALL win rate = 34.6% (net -10,533 INR).

rules.name: Require minimum gross premium movement for SENSEX trades
rules.conditionText: For SENSEX trades (BSE lot size = 10), require minimum gross premium target movement of 15 INR per unit (= 150 INR gross per lot) before entering. Round-trip transaction costs for SENSEX are ~83-90 INR per lot.

evidence.justification: Observed in 3 recent SENSEX TARGET_HIT trades with negative net_pnl due to friction costs.
